name: Souls of Mischief
hook: Four East Oakland teenagers whose one perfect single, built on a jazz-fusion drummer's record, became the sound of 1993.
blurb: A-Plus, Opio, Phesto and Tajai grew up in East Oakland and were part of Hieroglyphics, a group of rappers that also included Del the Funky Homosapien. In 1993, while still teenagers, they released '93 'til Infinity'. A-Plus built the beat from a 1974 record called 'Heather' by the drummer Billy Cobham, speeding up its slow bassline and marimba and adding his own drums. It is a relaxed, looping song about hanging out, and it shows the jazz-sample sound travelling west and staying separate from the gangsta rap that sold most in California in 1993. Its reputation has grown rather than faded: people still play it thirty years later, and it was fifth on Rolling Stone's 2023 list of the greatest West Coast hip-hop songs. Its beat is the first sample connection on this map whose source is a jazz-fusion record, which started the pattern of much-sampled source artists (Q21).
